surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the plasma polymerisation of DEPA* and TMP* followed by a nitrogen plasma step. The nitrogen plasma facilitates the incorporation of nitrogen into the phosphate structure, leading to the formation of P–N bonds. The process involves the removal of carbon groups at initial exposure, activation of the surface, and densification of the film during nitrogen plasma exposure. The nitrogen plasma also acts as an efficient step for carbon removal.
evidence: The surface reaction mechanism and associated chemistry are discussed in the context of plasma polymerisation of DEPA* and TMP*, the role of nitrogen plasma in incorporating nitrogen into the phosphate structure, and the formation of P–N bonds. The text describes the removal of carbon groups, activation of the surface, and densification of the film during nitrogen plasma exposure. The formation of P–O–P bonds and the role of surface hydroxyls and methoxy groups are also mentioned.
